jobs.description: Quantum Error Suppression and Error Mitigation Software | QESEM Skip to content Menu Product Back to main menu Product QESEM How it works Key innovations Who uses QESEM What's next News Wall Street Journal: IBM Claims New Era of ‘Quantum Advantage’ Partners & Platforms Back to main menu Partners & Platforms IBM Quantum / Qiskit Functions Quantinuum Other partners News Wall Street Journal: IBM Claims New Era of ‘Quantum Advantage’ Industries Back to main menu Industries Chemistry & pharma Materials & automotive Finance Government & national research HPC & national labs Other industries News Wall Street Journal: IBM Claims New Era of ‘Quantum Advantage’ Resources Back to main menu Resources Blog Research Videos News News Wall Street Journal: IBM Claims New Era of ‘Quantum Advantage’ Company Back to main menu Company About Leadership & team Trusted by Careers News Contact us News Wall Street Journal: IBM Claims New Era of ‘Quantum Advantage’ Get a demo Run larger quantum circuits, accurately & reliably QESEM (Quantum Error Suppression and Error Mitigation) software enables extraction of reliable results from noisy quantum processing units, giving you control over accuracy, circuit volume, and QPU time. Get a Demo View Documentation Five reasons teams use QESEM 01 Boost your circuit volumes Run larger and deeper circuits on the same underlying quantum hardware. QESEM’s noise-aware execution and error-management techniques extend the range of accurate computation available on noisy QPUs by orders of magnitude. 02 Trust your quantum results Validate and trust quantum results at scale with transparent methodologies, quantifiable confidence, and clear insight into their accuracy and how they were achieved. Lower-overhead extrapolated and heuristic approaches available. 03 Designed for any quantum hardware or application QESEM works as a general-purpose, application-agnostic layer across quantum applications and hardware modalities. It has been demonstrated on various platforms, such as IBM’s superconducting-qubit and Quantinuum’s trapped-ion systems. 04 Plan your QPU resources QESEM estimates the QPU resources required to achieve the requested accuracy before execution, giving you control over the accuracy–cost tradeoff. 05 Keep your existing workflow Continue writing circuits and observables in the tools you already use. Send your job to the QESEM API with your target accuracy and selected QPU; QESEM handles the hardware-aware execution workflow in the background. How It Works From circuit submission to validated results QESEM is an API-based middle layer between quantum algorithms and quantum hardware. It accepts a circuit, the observables to measure, the requested statistical accuracy, and the selected quantum processor. User qesem 1 Estimate resources + Estimate resources — details Send a circuit, observables, target precision, and selected QPU through the QESEM API. QESEM estimates the QPU time required to reach the requested accuracy. 2 Execute QESEM + Execute QESEM — details User reviews the estimate, adjusts the job, or approves the full run after defining the maximum resource allocation. 3 Suppress and mitigate + Suppress and mitigate — details QESEM applies gate optimization, noise-aware transpilation, error suppression, and error mitigation. The execution adapts to updated measurements and changing hardware conditions. 4 Receive Results + Receive Results — details QESEM returns the mitigated expectation values, statistical uncertainty, and execution metadata, including resource usage and comparison data. Key innovation components Noise-aware transpilation and operation selection Device and circuit characterization Gate optimization, dynamical decoupling, and twirling Adaptive execution with drift-aware updates Execution metrics for interpreting results Resource optimization for hybrid quantum-classical workloads Resource optimization for multi-observable workloads Multi-type quasi-probabilistic error mitigation Who uses QESEM For teams that work with quantum hardware QESEM is designed for users who have or will have access to a QPU and need to push beyond the accuracy or circuit-volume limits of unmitigated execution. Enterprise researchers in finance, chemistry, pharma, materials, etc. Quantum algorithm researchers and developers Hybrid quantum/classical supercomputing HPC centers Academic and national research groups Quantum hardware and platform providers 1 / 5 What’s next Building toward fault tolerant quantum computation Future fault-tolerant quantum computers will still involve residual errors, resource overhead, and performance tradeoffs. QESEM is designed to evolve in parallel with the development of the quantum hardware, extending from physical error suppression and mitigation toward logical error mitigation, hybrid quantum-classical workflows, and broader platform integrations. See what QESEM can do on your hardware of choice Bring your circuit, your target accuracy, and the QPU you want to use. Qedma can help you understand what is possible and how to get there. About IBM Quantum develops full-stack quantum computing hardware and software to advance quantum research and applications. Cooperation Qedma and IBM are collaborating to make quantum computing more accurate and practical. IBM is a strategic investor in Qedma Qedma’s QESEM error-reduction software is available through IBM’s Qiskit Functions Catalog IBM and Qedma recently announced a study demonstrating trusted quantum computation and quantum advantage … Read more + . Using QESEM on IBM Quantum Heron processors, researchers resolved complex, long-lived dynamics in a two-dimensional Floquet Ising model at up to 74 qubits, at a scale where leading classical approaches, including simulations on Fugaku, could not produce consistent results. The work was independently cross-validated on Quantinuum trapped-ion systems, reinforcing confidence that the observed physics was not device-specific. Read the announcement Read less − About Quantinuum’s quantum computing systems are among the most accurate based on average two-qubit gate fidelity. Cooperation Qedma is a founding member of the Quantinuum Startup Partner Program, and Qedma’s QESEM error mitigation software is commercially available to Quantinuum customers. The integration combines Quantinuum’s high-fidelity, trapped-ion systems with Qedma’s error reduction … Read more + technology to help users run larger and more complex workloads while maintaining target accuracy and managing resource use. The integration has been demonstrated on challenging workloads near the frontier of classical simulation, and Quantinuum hardware also provided independent cross-validation for the IBM-Qedma quantum-advantage study. Read the announcement Read less − About JSR Corporation is a technology company with chemistry at its core, developing advanced materials for semiconductors, displays, life sciences, and plastics. Cooperation JSR researchers used Qedma’s QESEM error-mitigation software to study point-group symmetries in many-electron molecular wavefunctions on IBM quantum hardware. In experiments using up to 32 qubits, QESEM produced the closest agreement with exact results, with a maximum discrepancy of only a few percent, supporting more reliable quantum simulations for chemistry and materials research. Read the paper About DESY is one of Germany’s largest research centers, conducting fundamental research in particle and high-energy physics, photon science and astroparticle physics. Cooperation DESY researchers, in collaboration with Qedma, developed and tested a practical method for extracting statistical properties directly from amplitude-encoded velocity fields, in the context of fluid dynamics simulations. Using QESEM on IBM’s ibm_fez processor, the researchers demonstrated … Read more + that central moments and structure functions can be recovered on current noisy hardware. Read the paper Another work by DESY uses QESEM to demonstrate quantum simulation of lattice quantum electrodynamics in 2+1 dimensions. Specifically the researchers developed an approach to compute properties of the model at different energy scales on the QPU which was demonstrated on real hardware experiments using QESEM. A paper describing the work and experimental results is currently under preparation. Read less − About The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) is a leading European hub for quantum research, focusing on applied quantum technology, photonics, sensors, and secure communication. Cooperation Qedma is collaborating with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and the University of Copenhagen on a quantum chemistry research project supported by the Eureka grant program. The project explores the potential energy surface of the water molecule using IBM quantum hardware … Read more + and Qedma’s QESEM error mitigation software, demonstrating how error mitigation can improve the accuracy of quantum chemistry calculations on today’s noisy processors while investigating the hardware capabilities required to achieve quantum advantage in chemistry. Read less − About LTM is a global technology consulting and digital solutions company. Cooperation Qedma and LTM are collaborating on QuEST, the Quantum Error Mitigated Statistical Training Library for High Impact Applications, with support from the India Israel Innovation Fund. The project is developing a modular quantum machine learning toolkit with built in error mitigation, designed to make QML more accessible and deliver more dependable performance on today’s NISQ hardware. About Hyundai Motor Company is a global automotive and mobility company investing in electrification, autonomous driving, connectivity, and future mobility technologies. Cooperation Qedma is working with Hyundai and academic collaborators on a proof of concept for q

Using QESEM on IBM Quantum Heron processors, researchers resolved complex, long-lived dynamics in a two-dimensional Floquet Ising model at up to 74 qubits, at a scale where leading classical approaches, including simulations on Fugaku, could not produce consistent results. Cooperation Qedma is a founding member of the Quantinuum Startup Partner Program, and Qedma’s QESEM error mitigation software is commercially available to Quantinuum customers. The integration combines Quantinuum’s high-fidelity, trapped-ion systems with Qedma’s error reduction … Read more + technology to help users run larger and more complex workloads while maintaining target accuracy and managing resource use. The integration has been demonstrated on challenging workloads near the frontier of classical simulation, and Quantinuum hardware also provided independent cross-validation for the IBM-Qedma quantum-advantage study.
